requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` is the shape of the JSON record. The text lists what it must identify: format version, run, project root, subject kind and full name, start time, backend and model, end time, outcome, determination, `evidence_output` and `evidence_written`. The reviewed root `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageRecord]` implements that shape. It derives `Serialize` and has `version`, `run_id`, `project_root`, `subject` and `subject_kind`. It also has `backend`, `model`, `start_time_ms`, `end_time_ms` (an `Option`, so it is absent until the run finishes), `outcome`, `determination` (an `Option`), `evidence_output` (a `&'static str`) and `evidence_written`. It has no field that could hold FIXME entry text, source text, prompts, responses or rationale. That matches the prohibitions on storing them. An alternative record that left out or renamed any of these fields would break the clause, so this root carries the structural obligation.

The other clauses describe observable behavior only:
- **Location:** the file sits under `<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`, one file per assessment. `UsageLog::start` builds that path and creates the file, and `save` rewrites it. The clause names no interface or library to use, so how the path is built is discretionary. The state root itself comes from `requirements.configuration.state_location`, which is cited and carries its own obligations.
- **Unfinished runs:** `start` writes outcome `unfinished` and `finish` sets the final outcome and end time. This is behavior, and the record's `outcome` and `end_time_ms` fields give the shape it needs.
- **Evidence destination and stdout mode:** `evidence_output` and `evidence_written` are values the code sets at run time. Keeping the record outside the project in stdout mode is also behavior.

No further implementation roots are needed.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.

- **Separate record per assessment at `<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`:**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported]` checks that the file lives under `habeas/authoring/usage` in the fixture state root. It also checks that the file name equals `<run_id>.json`.
  - The same test runs a second time and asserts the first record's bytes are unchanged and there are two files.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs]` and `#fn[confirm_runs_a_second_assessment_with_its_own_usage_record]` check one record per assessment.
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[citation_reviews_are_confirmed_with_fresh_targeted_conversations]` checks distinct run ids.
- **Required fields:**
  - The `usage_record_identifies_its_run...` test asserts `version` (3), `run_id`, `project_root`, `subject`, `subject_kind`, `backend`, `model`, `evidence_output`, and `start_time_ms <= end_time_ms`.
  - `src/authoring/usage.rs#fn[unfinished_runs_are_visible_before_the_backend_is_selected]` checks that backend, model and end time are null while the run is unfinished.
  - `usage_record_of_an_early_failure_identifies_its_subject_kind` checks null backend and model together with subject kind, failed outcome and an end time.
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[usage_subject_kind_is_known_before_sources_are_prepared]` covers the subject kinds.
- **Determination kind and `evidence_written`:**
  - The tests assert `determination` of `true`, `false` and `FIXME` in `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files`, `false_is_a_completed_assessment` and the Ollama CLI test.
  - They assert it is null when no determination was accepted, for example in `missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence`.
  - `evidence_written` is asserted true after a successful file write (the Ollama CLI test) and after a stdout write (the stdout test and `live_bedrock_authoring`).
  - It is asserted false after a failed write, where the accepted judgment is retained (`failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage`).
  - It is also asserted false after invalid submissions in both modes.
- **`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`:** `missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence` asserts both values. `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json...` and `usage_record_identifies_its_run...` assert `stdout` and `file` on successful runs.
- **Usage stays outside the project in stdout mode:** `usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it` runs with and without `--stdout` and a state root inside the project. It asserts the refusal message, empty stdout, and that the directory is not created.
- **FIXME entry text not stored:** the Ollama CLI test submits an `acknowledged_gap` with entry `example/app#125`. It asserts `#125` and the rationale are absent from the serialized usage record.
- **Failed, cancelled and unfinished runs are distinguishable:**
  - Unfinished is checked in the `unfinished_runs_are_visible...` test.
  - Failed outcomes are checked in the batch tests, the invalid-submission test and the early-failure test.
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[failed_persistence_records_failure_or_cancellation_and_retains_the_cause]` checks both `failed` and `cancelled`, with a null determination.
  - Completed runs have outcome `completed`.
- **No source text, prompts, responses or rationale stored:** the Ollama CLI test checks for requirement text, definition text, a source payload, the rationale and the credential in the serialized usage. `a_denied_read...` and the stdout test also keep usage content-free.
- **Cited `requirements.configuration.state_location`:** `usage_record_identifies_its_run...` checks that an unusable state location (a blocker file as `XDG_STATE_HOME`, or no home) is reported before any request and leaves existing evidence unchanged. The state root is resolved from the fixture state.

I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligation.

text: :::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
